title: GOD GIVING US OVER TO OUR CHOICE

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: That night God came to Balaam and said, "Since these men have come to summon you, go with them, but do only what I tell you." Balaam got up in the morning, saddled his donkey and went with the Moabite officials. - Num 22:20-21 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This night God gives Balaam a different answer. He tells him to go with the men, but only to do what God tells him. At first this seems confusing. Did God change His mind? Not at all. God's purpose for Israel never wavered; Israel would be blessed no matter what.

What we see here is something sobering. Balaam's heart was set on going, and God permitted him to follow the desire he refused to surrender. Sometimes God allows us to have what we insist upon, not because it is His best for us, but so that our own hearts are exposed. Permission is not the same as approval.

This is a solemn warning. We may pray until we hear the answer we want, mistaking God's permission for His blessing. But getting our way is not always a mercy. God may let us walk a road He never wanted for us, so that we learn the cost of an unsurrendered heart.

How much better to want what God wants from the start. In Christ we are invited to pray, as He did, "Not my will, but Yours be done" (Luke 22:42). That is the safest prayer we can ever pray. Do not press God for permission to walk your own way; ask instead for a heart that delights in His.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have you ever pressed God until you got the answer you wanted?
2. How do you tell the difference between God's permission and His blessing?
3. What would it mean to pray "Your will be done" and mean it fully?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, keep me from insisting on my own way until You let me have it. Teach me to pray "Your will be done" and to delight in what You desire for me. Amen.
